brief: Goldman delta-one desk head Rich Privorotsky opens the US week watching the yen, Hormuz and copper. Asian tech and semis ripped, SoftBank about 30% higher in three days on AGI expectations around OpenAI's Astra, with tech conferences and AI hardware earnings due to test whether spending intentions are still rising. KOSPI reversed a 2.5% gain to close lower despite record buybacks. The bigger surprise is the yen's sharp appreciation: stronger Japanese wage data reinforces the case for further BOJ tightening, which raises questions about a carry unwind hitting equities and credit, and leaves Japanese exporters underperforming on stronger currency plus higher energy. Energy stays his biggest risk. Iran's proposed exclusion zone could constrain ship to ship transfers, Vitol's Hardy puts Hormuz flows near 10m barrels a day with product markets tight, and Shanghai crude outperformance raises the question of China as marginal buyer. Iran-Oman talks near agreement but are not yet operational. Copper makes new LME highs on supply and tariff distortions, so not a clean growth signal, fitting a late cycle spending economy. With 61bps priced through next September he reads credibility hikes, not a cycle breaker, and would buy a CPI dip if the AI narrative holds.
